A table in a report is rarely a bare grid.
It carries a title, row names grouped into blocks, labels that span several columns, subtotals, source notes, and footnotes tied to particular cells.
Typst gives you a `table` element and leaves all of that to you, so the work becomes bookkeeping: which row is a subtotal, which cell needs a mark, which column of numbers lines up on its decimal point.

Keisen takes that bookkeeping.
You describe the parts and the formatting, and it builds the table.

_Keisen_ (罫線) is Japanese for the ruled lines of a table.

## Status

Keisen is in early development and has no release yet.
The API is being built milestone by milestone, and nothing on this site describes behaviour that does not exist: the [Reference](reference.qmd) and the [Examples](examples.qmd) fill in as each milestone lands.

Follow along in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/{{< var repository.slug >}}/issues), or read the [changelog](changelog.qmd).

## What it will do

Keisen implements the display-table grammar that R's [`gt`](https://gt.rstudio.com) and Python's [`great_tables`](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/) made familiar, designed for Typst rather than ported to it:

Parts
: A header, a stub with row names and groups, column labels with spanners, a body, summary rows, source notes, and footnotes whose marks are numbered in reading order.

Formatters
: A family covering numbers, integers, percentages, currency, scientific notation, dates, byte sizes, and markup, all computed in Typst's `decimal` type rather than in floats.

Locations
: Styling addressed by what the data says, so a cell is highlighted because its margin fell below a threshold, not because it is the fourth cell of the ninth row.

Nanoplots
: Sparklines and bars inside cells, sharing one domain down a column so they can be compared.

## Design

The core imports no third-party package, so formatting stays pluggable and installing Keisen pulls in nothing else.
Row groups are rendered as native repeating subheaders, which means a group that spans a page break reprints its label.
